newsitem.title: CHINA: China to use forex reserves to help state firms.
newsitem.headline: China to use forex reserves to help state firms.

text.p: China is expanding the use of its bulging foreign exchange reserves as credit for struggling state-owned enterprises, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The central government had endorsed four pilot projects to use $800 million in foreign exchange reserves as buyer's credit for companies threatened by increased competition from foreign firms, the newspaper said.
The pilot projects had benefited major power equipment producers and were expected to help the government assess the value of other uses for the reserves, the Business Weekly said.
"The government apparently is cautious about spreading the use of the reserves, but ministry officials said they believed the use in additional projects was under consideration," the newspaper said.

Measures to increase the use of the reserves were urgently needed because major state-owned machinery enterprises were losing market share to foreign firms and exports, it quoted Wang Jianye of the Ministry of Machine Building Industry as saying.
China's foreign exchange reserves stood at $115 billion at the end of April, up from $112.06 billion at the end of March, state media have reported.
